countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

courses.name: Bachelor of Liberal Arts
aliases: Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts
courses.summary: Bachelor of Liberal Arts is the Students Traffic catalogue category for multidisciplinary undergraduate degrees built around a declared major rather than a single fixed syllabus. O.P. Jindal Global University maps its four-year B.A. (Hons.) in Liberal Arts and Humanities at the Jindal School of Liberal Arts and Humanities to this category, a 196-credit degree with thirteen declared majors, a self-designed major option, five internships and a choice of research or coursework pathway in the final year.

courses.name: Bachelor of Design
courses.summary: Bachelor of Design is the catalogue category for four-year studio-based undergraduate design degrees. Lovely Professional University maps its B.Design Interior and Furniture programme, taught in English at Phagwara, to this category. The LPU version combines conceptual foundation coursework with intensive studio practice in interior and furniture design, adds design research methods and a dissertation, and allows an interdisciplinary minor. Other LPU B.Design tracks covering fashion, graphics, gaming, product and industrial design, and film and television production sit under the same category.

courses.name: Master of Business Administration
courses.summary: MBA is the Students Traffic catalogue category for full-time general-management master's degrees taken after a completed bachelor's degree. Lovely Professional University maps its two-year MBA, delivered in English across eight terms at the Phagwara campus and listed on the National Board of Accreditation Management PG register to 30 June 2027, to this category. LPU also runs specialised MBA tracks in areas such as international business, business analytics, supply chain and logistics, and hospital and healthcare management, which are admitted under separate programme codes.

universities.summary: FLAME University is a private, fully residential university for liberal education at Lavale, off the Pune-Bengaluru Highway in Pune, Maharashtra. Accredited A++ by NAAC in 2024, it teaches three- and four-year B.A., B.Sc., BBA and BBA (Communications Management) degrees with more than 24 majors, a four-year B.Des and a two-year MBA.
universities.campusLifestyle: FLAME is strictly residential, and exchange-student guidance states that all students must live on campus for the whole programme. The undergraduate programme offers more than 24 majors, each with at least eight matching minors, giving over 350 major-minor combinations. Campus facilities include dedicated learning spaces, sports facilities, recreation areas, a dining hall and several cafes. Every first-year undergraduate is assigned a faculty mentor and a peer mentor.
universities.cityProfile: The campus is at Gat No. 1270, Lavale, off the Pune-Bengaluru Highway, Pune 412115, Maharashtra. It is on a hill, and FLAME notes that Ola and Uber cabs can be irregular there. On working days FLAME runs five or six mini and medium buses from about 11:00 to 20:00, making around seven trips to Fergusson College Road (FC Road) in Pune city and back. Bus travel is included in the annual other fees. Serious medical cases are taken by 24-hour ambulance to Chellaram hospital.
universities.practicalExposure: The undergraduate curriculum includes foundation courses, major and minor specialisations, experiential learning courses, value-added courses, open electives and, in the optional fourth year, project-based courses. BBA (Communications Management) majors include Advertising and Branding, Digital Marketing and Communications, and Film and Television Management, while BBA majors include Finance, Business Analytics, Marketing, Operations and Entrepreneurship. FLAME's Career Services runs a placement process, training modules and a summer internship programme for undergraduate and postgraduate students. The Office of International Relations runs semester exchanges with partner universities, and FLAME also runs the FLAME Investment Lab and a summer immersion programme.
universities.hostelOverview: Housing is apartment-style twin sharing and is compulsory for the whole programme. The Year I lodging and boarding fee of INR 1,90,000 covers a twin room with a bathroom shared by flatmates, plus dining and laundry for up to 40 clothes a month. A room with an attached bathroom costs INR 94,000 more a year, and an air-conditioned room with an attached bathroom INR 1,41,000 more, allotted first come, first served. Students must be back on campus by midnight and inside their hostel by 02:00.
universities.dietarySupport: The dining hall serves vegetarian meals only, and breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner are included in the fees. Menus cover South Indian, North Indian, Maharashtrian, Chinese, Thai and Continental dishes, with live counters. Pay-and-eat cafes include Times Cafe, open until 02:00 with delivery, the Library Cafe and Juice Press.
universities.safetyOverview: Two residential doctors provide round-the-clock care. Of the three doctors, two are women, and students can choose to see a female doctor. A 24-hour ambulance transfers serious cases to Chellaram hospital. Students must be on campus by midnight and in their hostel by 02:00. FLAME has zero tolerance for drug abuse and can require urine, blood or breath tests.
universities.studentSupport: Four student counsellors, all clinical psychologists, work from 09:00 to 20:00 on working days. Every first-year undergraduate has a faculty mentor and a peer mentor, and from the second year a faculty advisor guides course choice, major and minor declaration and the degree audit. The Office of International Relations assigns student and faculty mentors to incoming exchange students.
whyChoose: Accredited A++ by NAAC, with a CGPA of 3.56 in its first accreditation cycle, declared in October 2024.
More than 24 majors and over 350 major-minor combinations, with a three-year degree and an optional fourth Honours year.
The whole admission process is online, including FEAT or FDAT, the essay and the interview, so international applicants do not need to travel to India to be assessed.
Published eligibility rules for IB Diploma, Cambridge A Level and accredited US high school diplomas, and SAT or ACT scores can replace FLAME's own entrance test.
Year-by-year fees are published for all four undergraduate years, including lodging, boarding and other charges, so the full cost of the degree can be planned.
Care on campus includes two residential doctors, the option of a female doctor, a 24-hour ambulance and four clinical-psychologist counsellors.
thingsToConsider: There is no dedicated international admissions page for degree students. International applicants go through the standard process, fees are published only in rupees, and the currency is confirmed in the offer letter.
Undergraduate and B.Des applicants must be under 21 on 31 July 2026, which rules out many gap-year or older applicants.
Qualifications other than IB, Cambridge A Level or an accredited US diploma need an equivalence certificate before you apply.
The dining hall is vegetarian only; other food is available only from pay-and-eat cafes.
The campus is on a hill outside the city. Cabs can be irregular and the free buses to FC Road run only from about 11:00 to 20:00.
The MBA accepts GMAT as the only non-Indian test, and admission for 2026 has closed.
bestFitFor: Students who want a liberal education with a wide choice of majors and minors, and who are happy to choose their degree title through their major.
IB, Cambridge A Level and US-system school leavers under 21 who want to apply entirely online with SAT, ACT or FEAT.
Design applicants with UCEED, NID or NIFT scores, or those willing to sit FLAME's own design aptitude test.
Graduates with a GMAT score who want a residential MBA with a published two-year cost.

faq.question: Is FLAME University public or private?
faq.answer: It is private. FLAME University was established as a state private university under the FLAME University Act 2014 (Maharashtra Act No. II of 2015), and the University Grants Commission lists it among the private universities of Maharashtra. Its sponsoring body is the Foundation for Liberal And Management Education Society.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: English. FLAME's Office of International Relations states that English is the language of instruction and examination in all courses except specific language courses, and that a minimum level of English proficiency is required. The degree admission pages do not name a specific IELTS or TOEFL score, and the essay, test and interview are all in English.

faq.question: Can I apply straight after finishing school with a foreign qualification?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are under 21 on 31 July 2026. FLAME accepts the full IB Diploma, a Cambridge A Level certificate with five O Level subjects at grades A to C including English plus three A Levels, and high school diplomas from accredited US-system schools. Other foreign school qualifications need an equivalence certificate submitted with the application.

faq.question: How much does the undergraduate programme cost?
faq.answer: For the incoming class of 2026, the published total is INR 11,45,000 in Year I, INR 11,95,000 in Year II, INR 12,50,000 in Year III and INR 13,00,000 in the optional Year IV. This covers the program fee, lodging and boarding with meals, and other fees. There is also a one-time INR 75,000 refundable caution deposit. Rooms with an attached bathroom or air conditioning cost INR 94,000 or INR 1,41,000 more a year.

faq.question: Do international students pay a different fee?
faq.answer: FLAME publishes one fee schedule for each programme, in rupees, and no separate foreign-national rate. It has no dedicated international admissions page for degree students, so international applicants should treat the rupee figures as a planning estimate. The offer letter confirms the fee and the currency of payment.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Register at apply.flame.edu.in, complete the online application with a statement of purpose, and pay the non-refundable INR 2,000 application fee online or by demand draft. Upload your Class 10 and Class 12 records. Shortlisted applicants take the online test and essay, then an online personal interview. You can keep your original passport as identity proof for the online assessment.

faq.question: Which entrance test do I need?
faq.answer: An admission test is mandatory. For the liberal education undergraduate programme, you take FLAME's online FEAT (120 minutes, no negative marking) or submit SAT or ACT scores, and SAT and ACT applicants write only the essay. For the B.Des, you take the FLAME Design Aptitude Test or submit UCEED, NID or NIFT scores. The MBA needs CAT, MAT, XAT, CMAT, NMAT, MH-CET or GMAT.

faq.question: When is the intake and when should I apply?
faq.answer: Undergraduate and B.Des students start in August; new undergraduates arrived on 7 to 9 August 2026. MBA students start in late July. For 2026 entry, undergraduate applications ran in six online cycles from 30 November 2025 to 21 June 2026. Applying in an early cycle gets you an earlier decision and more time for a student visa, which FLAME says can take up to eight weeks.

faq.question: Is FLAME accredited?
faq.answer: Yes. NAAC accredited FLAME University with grade A++ and a CGPA of 3.56 in its first cycle, as declared by NAAC's 220th Standing Committee in October 2024. The UGC lists it among Maharashtra's private universities. How the degree is recognised abroad depends on the credential-evaluation body in your destination country.

faq.question: What is accommodation like?
faq.answer: Living on campus is compulsory for the whole programme. Rooms are apartment-style twin shares with a bathroom shared by flatmates, included in the INR 1,90,000 Year I lodging and boarding fee with meals and laundry. Rooms with an attached bathroom or air conditioning cost more and are allotted first come, first served. Students must be on campus by midnight and in their hostel by 02:00.

faq.question: Are scholarships available?
faq.answer: FLAME awards merit scholarships at admission, ranging from partial to full fee waivers, based mainly on your final internal admission score, and the amount appears in the offer letter. There are also special scholarships for rank holders and sports achievers. The FLAME Fellows Program gives 20 full tuition waivers to postgraduate students with CAT or XAT above the 90th percentile or GMAT above 650. Emergency need-based support is also available.

faq.question: Can international graduates apply for the MBA?
faq.answer: Yes, if they hold a bachelor's degree with at least 50 per cent aggregate from a university recognised by the UGC or an equivalent body, and a valid test score. The GMAT, valid for five years, is the practical route for most international applicants. Selection adds an essay, an online interview, a 60-second video and personality profiling. Admission for 2026 has closed.

The FLAME Fellows Program offers 20 full tuition waivers to postgraduate students with CAT or XAT above the 90th percentile, or a GMAT score above 650.

teachingPhases.details: Residential MBA at the FLAME School of Business. First-year students arrive on 30 July 2026, followed by induction and orientation to 16 August 2026.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.
